Appearance:
 Shri Pankaj Chandra Bagadiya, counsel for the applica
 Shri Jayesh Yadav appearing on behalf of Advocate Gen
 Order

This petition under section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the applicant praying for the following reliefs :-
(i) to set aside the order dated 1.10.2021 passed in Cr.Revision No. 6/2021 passed by District & Sessions Judge, Jhabua.
(ii) to set aside the order dated 18.1.2021 passed by JMFC, Jhabua in criminal case No. 1923 of 2014 rejecting the application of applicant under section 77 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006.

(iii) to quash the proceedings of criminal case No.
(iv) to quash the impugned order of taking cognizance dated 18.11.2014 by JMFC,
Jhabua in cr.case No. 1923/2014.
2.
Counsel for the applicant submits that sample was taken by the 2 MCRC-53269-2021 Food Safety Officer on 14.09.2011.
Sample was sent to Food Analyst on 15.09.2011.
Report of the Public Analyst was received on 30.09.2011.
Report of Referral Food Laborartory is dated 3.1.2012.
The designated Officer has granted sanction on 7.12.2013 and complaint was filed before the trial court on 18.11.2014.

Learned counsel inviting attention of this Court to the chronology as aforesaid, submits that complaint in the instant case has been filed on 18.11.2014 after more than 3 years from the date of alleged offence i.e. 14.9.2011.

As per section 77 of the Act, the cognizance can be taken within a period of one year from the date of offence, however the Commissioner of Food Safety may for reasons to be recorded in writing approve prosecution within an extended period upto 3 years.

To boldster his submissions, counsel has placed reliance on the following orders :-

sentences.text:
4. To appreciate the controversy, it is apposite to refer section 77 of the Act which reads as under :-
3 MCRC-53269-2021 "Section 77. Time limit for prosecution :-
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, no court shall take cognizance of an offfence under this Act after the expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of an offence:
Provided that the Commissioner of Food Safety may, for reasons to be recorded in writing approve prosecution within an extended period up to three years."
5.
The aforesaid provision prescribes that the limitation period has to be counted from the date of offence and not from the date of report of food analyst or from the date of sanction of prosecution.
All these formalities are required to be completed within a period of one year from the date of commission of offence so that the accused may not be adversely affected.

The object of prescribing the period of limitation has been clarified by the Hon'ble appex court in the case State of Punjab vs Sarwan Singh, AIR 1981 SC 1054 wherein it is held that in putting a bar of limitation on prosecutions was clearly to prevent the parties from filing cases after a long time, as a result of which material evidence may disappear and also to prevent abuse of the process of the court by filing vexatious and belated prosecution long after the date of the offence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is therefore of the utmost importance that any prosecution, whether by the State or a private complainant must abide by the letter of law or take the risk of the prosecution failing on the ground of limitation.
The aforesaid submission finds support from the above referred judgments relied on by the counsel for the applicant.

In the instant case, 4 MCRC-53269-2021 clearly the date of offence is 14/09/2011 and complaint has been filed after more than three year from the date of offence which is clearly barred Deendayal Somani S/O Banshilal Somani ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50340034/
2 by limitation.

sentences.text: In view aforesaid object and limitation of prosecution, learned court below has failed to appreciate the provision of limitation as enshrined under section 77 of the Act.
The order passed by courts below are not sustainable as it would lead to miscarriage of justice.
Hence this petition is allowed and the impugned orders dated 18.1.2021 passed in cr.case No. 1923/2014 and 1.10.2021 passed in Cr.Revision No. 6/2021 are set aside.
Applicant is discharged for the charge levelled against him.
Copy of the order be sent to the concerned court.
